summary: Sacks contextualizes the H20 export ban, noting that memory bandwidth — where the H20 actually exceeds the H100 by 20% — matters more than raw flops in the new AI paradigm, making the chip 'frankly too good' to sell to China; he supports export controls but frames this as a line-drawing question rather than a company-level investment call.
quote: If you look at the memory bandwidth on the H20, it actually has 20% more memory bandwidth than the H100. So I think there's a view that this chip is just frankly too good.
